PAGE 1: Numerator and denominator
NUMERATOR AND DENOMINATOR
====

A fraction shows a part of a whole. If a chapati is cut into 4 equal pieces and you eat 1 piece, you have eaten one quarter of the chapati. We write one quarter as 1/4.

Every fraction has two numbers. The bottom number is the denominator. It tells us how many equal parts the whole is cut into. The top number is the numerator. It tells us how many of those parts we are talking about.

In the fraction 3/4:
• The denominator is 4: the whole is cut into 4 equal parts.
• The numerator is 3: we take 3 of those parts.

### The parts must be equal
A fraction only works when the parts are equal in size. If a cake is cut into one big piece and two small pieces, we cannot say each piece is one third.

### Reading fractions
• 1/2 is read one half.
• 1/4 is read one quarter.
• 3/4 is read three quarters.
• 5/8 is read five eighths.
• 7/10 is read seven tenths.

### Try it
In 5/8, the numerator is 5 and the denominator is 8. It means 5 out of 8 equal parts.

PAGE 2: Fractions as part of a whole
FRACTIONS AS PART OF A WHOLE
====

A whole can be a circle, a rectangle, a rope, a piece of paper or even a clock face. To show a fraction, cut the whole into equal parts equal to the denominator, and colour the number of parts equal to the numerator.

### Fractions on a clock face
A clock face is a circle with 12 equal spaces for the hours. Half an hour is 30 minutes, which is 1/2 of an hour. A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes, which is 1/4 of an hour. Each hour mark is 1/12 of the clock face.

### Cutting paper
Take a strip of paper. Fold it in half, then in half again and again. You get halves, quarters and eighths. Each time you fold, the parts get smaller, but they are still equal.

### Example
A rope is cut into 10 equal pieces and Amina takes 7 of them. She has 7/10 of the rope.

### Check yourself
Draw a rectangle and cut it into 12 equal parts. Shade 5 parts. The fraction shaded is 5/12. The fraction not shaded is 7/12. Together they make 12/12, which is one whole.

PAGE 3: Fractions as part of a group
FRACTIONS AS PART OF A GROUP
====

A fraction can also describe part of a group of things, like 3 out of 4 pupils or 5 out of 12 goats. The denominator shows how many equal groups we split the collection into. The numerator shows how many of the groups we take.

Find 3/4 of 12 counters.

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Figure 3: Three quarters of a group of 12 counters
ALT: Twelve counters in four rows of three, with three of the four rows shaded, making 9 shaded counters
PAYLOAD:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 320 196" width="320" height="196" role="img">
<circle cx="126" cy="37" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="160" cy="37" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="194" cy="37" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="126" cy="71" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="160" cy="71" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="194" cy="71" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="126" cy="105" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="160" cy="105" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="194" cy="105" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="126" cy="139" r="12" fill="#fff" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="160" cy="139" r="12" fill="#fff" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="194" cy="139" r="12" fill="#fff" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="160" y="182" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" fill="#111">3 of the 4 rows are shaded: 9 counters</text>
</svg>
CAPTION: Figure 3: Three quarters of a group of 12 counters
[/DIAGRAM]
Step 1: Divide the group by the denominator: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. This is one quarter of the group.
Step 2: Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 3 = 9.
So 3/4 of 12 is 9.

### Another example
Wafula has 20 goats. 1/5 of them are brown. How many are brown?
Step 1: 20 ÷ 5 = 4.
Step 2: 1 × 4 = 4.
There are 4 brown goats.

### Part of a group in a class
A class has 30 pupils. 2/5 of them walk to school. Divide 30 by 5 to get 6. Multiply by 2 to get 12. So 12 pupils walk.

### Remember
Fractions of a group are always whole numbers here. Use your division facts to find them quickly.

PAGE 4: Proper, improper and mixed fractions
PROPER, IMPROPER AND MIXED FRACTIONS
====

There are three kinds of fractions.

### Proper fractions
In a proper fraction, the numerator is smaller than the denominator. It is less than one whole. Examples: 1/2, 3/4, 5/8.

### Improper fractions
In an improper fraction, the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. It is one whole or more. Examples: 5/4, 7/3, 9/9.

### Mixed fractions
A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction together. Example: 1 3/4, read one and three quarters.

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Figure 4: 1 3/4 shown as 7/4
ALT: Two bars each cut into four equal parts: the first fully shaded and the second with three parts shaded, showing one and three quarters, which is seven quarters
PAYLOAD:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 410 114" width="410" height="114" role="img">
<text x="82" y="30" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#111">1 whole</text>
<rect x="90" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="165" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="240" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>

</svg>
CAPTION: Figure 4: 1 3/4 shown as 7/4
[/DIAGRAM]
The picture shows 4 quarters and then 3 more quarters. That is 7 quarters in all. So 1 3/4 and 7/4 are two ways of writing the same amount.

### Sorting fractions
• 2/9 is proper (2 is less than 9).
• 11/5 is improper (11 is more than 5).
• 3 1/2 is mixed (a whole number 3 and a fraction 1/2).
• 8/8 is improper, and equals 1 whole.

### Example
A jug holds 1/4 of a litre when full. Three full jugs of juice make 3/4 of a litre.

PAGE 5: Changing improper fractions to mixed fractions
CHANGING IMPROPER FRACTIONS TO MIXED FRACTIONS
====

An improper fraction can be written as a mixed fraction. To do this, divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number. The remainder becomes the new numerator. The denominator stays the same.

Change 11/4 to a mixed fraction.

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Figure 5: 11/4 drawn as 2 wholes and 3/4
ALT: Three bars cut into quarters: two fully shaded bars and one bar with three quarters shaded, showing eleven quarters which is two and three quarters
PAYLOAD:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 410 166" width="410" height="166" role="img">
<text x="82" y="30" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#111">4/4</text>
<rect x="90" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="165" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>

CAPTION: Figure 5: 11/4 drawn as 2 wholes and 3/4
[/DIAGRAM]
Step 1: Divide 11 by 4. 11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3.
Step 2: The quotient 2 is the whole number.
Step 3: The remainder 3 is the numerator and 4 stays as the denominator.
Answer: 11/4 = 2 3/4.

### More examples
• 7/3: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1, so 7/3 = 2 1/3.
• 23/6: 23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5, so 23/6 = 3 5/6.
• 8/4: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 0, so 8/4 = 2. There is no fraction part.

### Check
Turn the answer back: 2 3/4 has 2 wholes, each with 4 quarters, making 8 quarters, plus 3 quarters makes 11 quarters.

### Example
Njoki has 9 halves of oranges. 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1, so she has 4 1/2 oranges.

PAGE 6: Changing mixed fractions to improper fractions
CHANGING MIXED FRACTIONS TO IMPROPER FRACTIONS
====

To change a mixed fraction to an improper fraction, we find how many equal parts there are altogether. Multiply the whole number by the denominator, then add the numerator. The denominator stays the same.

Change 3 2/5 to an improper fraction.

<rect x="90" y="164" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>

</svg>
CAPTION: Figure 6: 3 2/5 drawn in fifths
[/DIAGRAM]
Step 1: Multiply the whole number by the denominator: 3 × 5 = 15. There are 15 fifths in 3 wholes.
Step 2: Add the numerator: 15 + 2 = 17.
Step 3: Keep the denominator 5.
Answer: 3 2/5 = 17/5.

### More examples
• 2 1/3: 2 × 3 = 6, 6 + 1 = 7, so 7/3.
• 4 3/8: 4 × 8 = 32, 32 + 3 = 35, so 35/8.
• 1 5/6: 1 × 6 = 6, 6 + 5 = 11, so 11/6.

### Going both ways
Changing improper to mixed uses division. Changing mixed to improper uses multiplication and addition. They undo each other. Check: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2, which gives 3 2/5 again.

### Common mistakes
• Changing the denominator. It never changes in these conversions.
• Forgetting to add the numerator after multiplying.
• Writing the remainder as the whole number instead of the quotient.
pages.quiz:
MATHEMATICS — FRACTIONS · REVISION QUIZ
====

Answer in your exercise book. Show your working. Then check with the Answers tab.

1. In the fraction 5/8, which number is the denominator?
   A. 5
   B. 8
   C. 13
   D. 3

2. Which of these is an improper fraction?
   A. 3/8
   B. 7/4
   C. 2 1/2
   D. 1/10

3. What is 3/4 of 12?
   A. 3
   B. 4
   C. 9
   D. 16

4. Change 11/4 to a mixed fraction.
   A. 2 1/4
   B. 2 3/4
   C. 3 1/4
   D. 3 3/4

5. Change 3 2/5 to an improper fraction.
   A. 5/17
   B. 15/5
   C. 17/5
   D. 32/5

6. A rectangle is cut into 12 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded. What fraction is shaded and what fraction is not shaded? (2 marks)

7. Wafula has 20 goats and 1/5 of them are brown. How many goats are brown? Show your working. (3 marks)

8. Change 23/6 to a mixed fraction. (3 marks)

9. Write 4 3/8 as an improper fraction. (3 marks)

10. Explain why the parts must be equal when we write 1/3. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — FRACTIONS · ANSWERS
====

1. B
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows the whole is cut into 8 equal parts.

2. B
   In 7/4 the numerator 7 is bigger than the denominator 4. 3/8 and 1/10 are proper, and 2 1/2 is mixed.

3. C
   12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 3 × 3 = 9.

4. B
   11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3, so 11/4 = 2 3/4.

5. C
   3 × 5 = 15 and 15 + 2 = 17. The denominator stays 5, so the answer is 17/5.

6. 5/12 is shaded and 7/12 is not shaded.
   1 mark for 5/12. The unshaded parts are 12 − 5 = 7, so 1 mark for 7/12.

7. 4 goats
   20 ÷ 5 = 4 (2 marks for correct working) and 1 × 4 = 4 goats (1 mark).

8. 3 5/6
   23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5 (2 marks). So 23/6 = 3 5/6 with the denominator unchanged (1 mark).

9. 35/8
   4 × 8 = 32 (1 mark); 32 + 3 = 35 (1 mark); keep the denominator 8 to give 35/8 (1 mark).

10. A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. If the parts are different sizes, one piece is not one third.
   1 mark for saying the parts must be equal in size and 1 mark for the reasoning that the denominator counts equal parts.

studyPages.title: Numerator and denominator
studyPages.body:
NUMERATOR AND DENOMINATOR
====

A fraction shows a part of a whole. If a chapati is cut into 4 equal pieces and you eat 1 piece, you have eaten one quarter of the chapati. We write one quarter as 1/4.

Every fraction has two numbers. The bottom number is the denominator. It tells us how many equal parts the whole is cut into. The top number is the numerator. It tells us how many of those parts we are talking about.

In the fraction 3/4:
• The denominator is 4: the whole is cut into 4 equal parts.
• The numerator is 3: we take 3 of those parts.

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Figure 1: Fraction bars showing 1/2, 1/4, 3/4 and 5/8
ALT: Four equal-length bars cut into 2, 4, 4 and 8 equal parts, with 1, 1, 3 and 5 parts shaded

[/DIAGRAM]
### The parts must be equal
A fraction only works when the parts are equal in size. If a cake is cut into one big piece and two small pieces, we cannot say each piece is one third.

### Reading fractions
• 1/2 is read one half.
• 1/4 is read one quarter.
• 3/4 is read three quarters.
• 5/8 is read five eighths.
• 7/10 is read seven tenths.

### Try it
In 5/8, the numerator is 5 and the denominator is 8. It means 5 out of 8 equal parts.

studyPages.title: Fractions as part of a whole
studyPages.body:
FRACTIONS AS PART OF A WHOLE
====

A whole can be a circle, a rectangle, a rope, a piece of paper or even a clock face. To show a fraction, cut the whole into equal parts equal to the denominator, and colour the number of parts equal to the numerator.

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Figure 2: Circles cut into equal parts with some parts shaded
ALT: Three circles, the first cut into 8 parts with 3 shaded, the second into 4 parts with 1 shaded, and the third into 6 parts with 5 shaded

### Fractions on a clock face
A clock face is a circle with 12 equal spaces for the hours. Half an hour is 30 minutes, which is 1/2 of an hour. A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes, which is 1/4 of an hour. Each hour mark is 1/12 of the clock face.

### Cutting paper
Take a strip of paper. Fold it in half, then in half again and again. You get halves, quarters and eighths. Each time you fold, the parts get smaller, but they are still equal.

### Example
A rope is cut into 10 equal pieces and Amina takes 7 of them. She has 7/10 of the rope.

### Check yourself
Draw a rectangle and cut it into 12 equal parts. Shade 5 parts. The fraction shaded is 5/12. The fraction not shaded is 7/12. Together they make 12/12, which is one whole.

studyPages.title: Fractions as part of a group
studyPages.body:
FRACTIONS AS PART OF A GROUP
====

A fraction can also describe part of a group of things, like 3 out of 4 pupils or 5 out of 12 goats. The denominator shows how many equal groups we split the collection into. The numerator shows how many of the groups we take.

Find 3/4 of 12 counters.

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Figure 3: Three quarters of a group of 12 counters
ALT: Twelve counters in four rows of three, with three of the four rows shaded, making 9 shaded counters
PAYLOAD:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 320 196" width="320" height="196" role="img">
<circle cx="126" cy="37" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="160" cy="37" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="194" cy="37" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="126" cy="71" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="160" cy="71" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="194" cy="71" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="126" cy="105" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="160" cy="105" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="194" cy="105" r="12" fill="#ef6c00" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>

<circle cx="194" cy="139" r="12" fill="#fff" stroke="#e65100" stroke-width="2"/>

</svg>
CAPTION: Figure 3: Three quarters of a group of 12 counters
[/DIAGRAM]
Step 1: Divide the group by the denominator: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. This is one quarter of the group.
Step 2: Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 3 = 9.
So 3/4 of 12 is 9.

### Another example
Wafula has 20 goats. 1/5 of them are brown. How many are brown?
Step 1: 20 ÷ 5 = 4.
Step 2: 1 × 4 = 4.
There are 4 brown goats.

### Part of a group in a class
A class has 30 pupils. 2/5 of them walk to school. Divide 30 by 5 to get 6. Multiply by 2 to get 12. So 12 pupils walk.

### Remember
Fractions of a group are always whole numbers here. Use your division facts to find them quickly.

studyPages.title: Proper, improper and mixed fractions
studyPages.body:
PROPER, IMPROPER AND MIXED FRACTIONS
====

There are three kinds of fractions.

### Proper fractions
In a proper fraction, the numerator is smaller than the denominator. It is less than one whole. Examples: 1/2, 3/4, 5/8.

### Improper fractions
In an improper fraction, the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. It is one whole or more. Examples: 5/4, 7/3, 9/9.

### Mixed fractions
A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction together. Example: 1 3/4, read one and three quarters.

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Figure 4: 1 3/4 shown as 7/4
ALT: Two bars each cut into four equal parts: the first fully shaded and the second with three parts shaded, showing one and three quarters, which is seven quarters
PAYLOAD:

<text x="82" y="30" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#111">1 whole</text>
<rect x="90" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="165" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="240" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="315" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="82" y="82" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#111">3/4 more</text>
<rect x="90" y="60" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="165" y="60" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>

<rect x="315" y="60" width="75" height="34" fill="#fff" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>

</svg>
CAPTION: Figure 4: 1 3/4 shown as 7/4
[/DIAGRAM]
The picture shows 4 quarters and then 3 more quarters. That is 7 quarters in all. So 1 3/4 and 7/4 are two ways of writing the same amount.

### Sorting fractions
• 2/9 is proper (2 is less than 9).
• 11/5 is improper (11 is more than 5).
• 3 1/2 is mixed (a whole number 3 and a fraction 1/2).
• 8/8 is improper, and equals 1 whole.

### Example
A jug holds 1/4 of a litre when full. Three full jugs of juice make 3/4 of a litre.

studyPages.title: Changing improper fractions to mixed fractions
studyPages.body:
CHANGING IMPROPER FRACTIONS TO MIXED FRACTIONS
====

An improper fraction can be written as a mixed fraction. To do this, divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number. The remainder becomes the new numerator. The denominator stays the same.

Change 11/4 to a mixed fraction.

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Figure 5: 11/4 drawn as 2 wholes and 3/4
ALT: Three bars cut into quarters: two fully shaded bars and one bar with three quarters shaded, showing eleven quarters which is two and three quarters
PAYLOAD:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 410 166" width="410" height="166" role="img">
<text x="82" y="30" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#111">4/4</text>
<rect x="90" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="165" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="240" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="315" y="8" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="82" y="82" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#111">4/4</text>
<rect x="90" y="60" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="165" y="60" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="240" y="60" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="315" y="60" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="82" y="134" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#111">3/4</text>
<rect x="90" y="112" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="165" y="112" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="240" y="112" width="75" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="315" y="112" width="75" height="34" fill="#fff" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>

</svg>
CAPTION: Figure 5: 11/4 drawn as 2 wholes and 3/4
[/DIAGRAM]
Step 1: Divide 11 by 4. 11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3.
Step 2: The quotient 2 is the whole number.
Step 3: The remainder 3 is the numerator and 4 stays as the denominator.
Answer: 11/4 = 2 3/4.

### More examples
• 7/3: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1, so 7/3 = 2 1/3.
• 23/6: 23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5, so 23/6 = 3 5/6.
• 8/4: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 0, so 8/4 = 2. There is no fraction part.

### Check
Turn the answer back: 2 3/4 has 2 wholes, each with 4 quarters, making 8 quarters, plus 3 quarters makes 11 quarters.

### Example
Njoki has 9 halves of oranges. 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1, so she has 4 1/2 oranges.

studyPages.title: Changing mixed fractions to improper fractions
studyPages.body:
CHANGING MIXED FRACTIONS TO IMPROPER FRACTIONS
====

To change a mixed fraction to an improper fraction, we find how many equal parts there are altogether. Multiply the whole number by the denominator, then add the numerator. The denominator stays the same.

Change 3 2/5 to an improper fraction.

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Figure 6: 3 2/5 drawn in fifths
ALT: Four bars cut into fifths: three fully shaded bars and one bar with two fifths shaded, making seventeen fifths
PAYLOAD:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 410 218" width="410" height="218" role="img">
<text x="82" y="30" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#111">1</text>
<rect x="90" y="8" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="150" y="8" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="210" y="8" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="270" y="8" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>

<rect x="330" y="60" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="82" y="134" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#111">1</text>
<rect x="90" y="112" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="150" y="112" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="210" y="112" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="270" y="112" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="330" y="112" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="82" y="186" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#111">2/5</text>
<rect x="90" y="164" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="150" y="164" width="60" height="34" fill="#90caf9" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="210" y="164" width="60" height="34" fill="#fff" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="270" y="164" width="60" height="34" fill="#fff" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="330" y="164" width="60" height="34" fill="#fff" stroke="#0d47a1" stroke-width="2"/>

</svg>
CAPTION: Figure 6: 3 2/5 drawn in fifths
[/DIAGRAM]
Step 1: Multiply the whole number by the denominator: 3 × 5 = 15. There are 15 fifths in 3 wholes.
Step 2: Add the numerator: 15 + 2 = 17.
Step 3: Keep the denominator 5.
Answer: 3 2/5 = 17/5.

### More examples
• 2 1/3: 2 × 3 = 6, 6 + 1 = 7, so 7/3.
• 4 3/8: 4 × 8 = 32, 32 + 3 = 35, so 35/8.
• 1 5/6: 1 × 6 = 6, 6 + 5 = 11, so 11/6.

### Going both ways
Changing improper to mixed uses division. Changing mixed to improper uses multiplication and addition. They undo each other. Check: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2, which gives 3 2/5 again.

### Common mistakes
• Changing the denominator. It never changes in these conversions.
• Forgetting to add the numerator after multiplying.
• Writing the remainder as the whole number instead of the quotient.
